conversionProcess.issue: Converting hydraulic models from one program to another requires a degree of dedication due to the intricacies involved in the process. It requires a certain investment of time and an understanding of both programs. This series of articles contains step-by-step instructions to perform a basic conversion for the BASE scenario from InfoSewer to InfoWorks ICM.
conversionProcess.disclaimer: Please be aware that this guide is not exhaustive. The unique setup of each InfoSewer model means a one-size-fits-all approach to conversion is impractical. However, these steps have been carefully planned to facilitate the conversion process for as many models as possible.
highLevelSteps: Converting DBF Files to CSV: Use an Excel macro to convert DBF files within the .IEDB model folder to CSV format for importing network data into ICM.
Converting Map.mdb to SHP: Use ESRI's ArcCatalog to convert the Map.mdb file within the .IEDB model folder to SHP format for importing network geometry into ICM.
Importing CSV Files: Import network data from CSV files with configuration (CFG) files.
Importing SHP Files: Import geometry data from SHP files with configuration (CFG) files.
Performing Data Manipulation: Modify imported data using SQL.
rubyScriptInputs: Folder containing converted SHP files from Map.mdb
Folder containing converted CSV files from .IEDB
conversionProcess.importantNote: Verify that display units are set as desired prior to import. To review units in ICM, go to Tools > Options and view the Units tab. Display units can be modified as necessary.

implementationSteps: Project Creation: Open ArcMap with appropriate coordinate system, load background layers/shapefiles, initialize new InfoSewer project
Database Initialization: System creates IEDB folder structure, default tables populated with standard fields, spatial reference system established
Data Population: Import existing network data (CSV/Geodatabase), manual data entry through attribute browsers, bulk data updates via DB Editor
Configuration Optimization: Set display scopes and domains, configure custom fields for project needs, establish data validation rules
Network Validation: Run 'Update Map from DB' to sync database with map, perform connectivity checks, validate hydraulic parameters
